clue.text: Pep plutarch displayed in piece of ornate prose

indicators.note: the letters are laid out afresh, put on show in a new order

explanation.surface: Some words by the Greek biographer Plutarch are shown off in an elaborate passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' signals an anagram of PEP PLUTARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A florid, over-written passage in a piece of writing is called this, from Horace's phrase about patches of purple cloth.

clue.text: Dad, Rex and carol are doing grammar exercises

parts.note: dad is pa, an informal word for father
Rex, Latin for king, is abbreviated R
to carol is to sing

explanation.surface: A father, a king and a carol singer are all busy with grammar homework.
explanation.definitionFit: Analysing a sentence into its parts of speech is a classic school grammar exercise.

clue.text: Regret including English quintet in show

indicators.note: the word for regret holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a quintet is five, which is V in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A remorseful English five-piece band appears in a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: A light theatrical entertainment of sketches and songs is a kind of stage show.

clue.text: Pal idly destroys a leaf

indicators.note: destroying something breaks it up, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A lazy friend wrecks a leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroys' signals an anagram of PAL IDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The broad floating pad of a water plant is its leaf.

clue.text: Favoured university faces a plant

indicators.note: faces means comes in front of, so these pieces sit before the final letter

parts.note: a favoured person is a pet

explanation.surface: A favourite university confronts a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flowering plant with trumpet-shaped blooms, often grown in baskets.

clue.text: Demanding task for fraternity of high standing

explanation.surface: A hard job for a respected brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult undertaking is an idiom for a big ask; read literally, a tall religious order is a lofty brotherhood.

clue.text: Crazy Henry always takes the telegraph

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
ay (or aye) is an old word meaning always
a wire is a telegram, and telegraph means to send one

explanation.surface: A mad man named Henry always reads this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the telegraph' looks like the newspaper but means a wire, an old word for telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: Going haywire is an idiom for behaving wildly or out of control.

clue.text: Dry up and give novice absolution

explanation.surface: A priest's instruction to wither and to forgive a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as SHRIVE, to give absolution, and L for learner, a novice, as on British learner-driver plates.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither as moisture leaves is to dry up; read cryptically, absolving (shriving) a learner gives the same letters.

clue.text: Unhappy results of taking team property

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
personal effects are a person's property

explanation.surface: Bad consequences of seizing a club's assets.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwanted secondary consequences of a medicine are what one may suffer from taking it.

clue.text: The call of the countryside

parts.note: reads like the lure of rural life, but means a shout heard in the countryside, the huntsman's cry on sighting a fox

explanation.definitionFit: The cry raised in fox hunting when the quarry is seen.

clue.text: Spell of bowling may cause excessive strain

parts.note: an over is a bowler's set of six balls in cricket
a stretch is a spell or period of time

explanation.surface: A long spell of bowling might cause a cricketer to pull a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To push something beyond its limits is to strain it too far.

clue.text: Chauffeur needs motivation

explanation.surface: A driver needs a reason to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To chauffeur someone is to take them by car; ambition or push is also called this.

clue.text: Entertainment in which I'm top name, anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old way, so the letters are put in a random order

explanation.surface: A star boasts of top billing in some show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' signals an anagram of I'M TOP NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A British Christmas stage show for families, with a dame and slapstick.

clue.text: Bound to be given a job

explanation.surface: Someone sure to be hired.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple pledged to marry are bound to be wed; someone hired has been taken on for work.

clue.text: Maybe get singer to accept compliments

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible version of these letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Perhaps persuade a vocalist to take praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals an anagram of GET SINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Compliments in the sense of polite good wishes, as in 'with the compliments of'.

clue.text: Speech on where one lives

explanation.surface: A talk about one's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk to an audience; also the details of a home's location used for post.

clue.text: Wallets made by origami fans

explanation.surface: Paper wallets made by Japanese paper-folding enthusiasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper wallets that hold documents; and people who crease paper, as origami enthusiasts do.

clue.text: Rope in many an investigative force

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
taken as written
the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters

explanation.surface: Many police officers are roped in to an investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard, often just 'the Yard', is the London police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord worn round the neck or a short rope used on ships for fastening.

clue.text: I can't remember who wants standing orders

explanation.surface: A forgetful person wanting regular payment arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: A placeholder phrase for someone whose name escapes one; and a bank's standing orders are SOs, one and another.

clue.text: Inquest oficial put top obstetrician in a spot

indicators.note: the first letter of obstetrician is placed inside the word for a spot

parts.note: to be in a spot is to be in a corner, a tight place

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An official at an inquest puts a leading doctor in a difficult position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oficial' is the clue's misprint for official.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who investigates sudden or unexplained deaths at an inquest.

clue.text: Diplomacy needed by Tory association

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
tact is diplomacy in handling people

explanation.surface: Diplomacy is required for Conservative alliances.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in touch or connected with someone is a synonym of association.

clue.text: No single section is offensive

parts.note: taken as written
I is one, as a Roman numeral
some means a part or section of a whole

explanation.surface: Not one part is objectionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A noxious, foul-smelling thing is offensive to the senses.

clue.text: Compel prisoners to go by rail

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners
a train runs on rail

explanation.surface: Inmates are forced to travel by train.
explanation.definitionFit: To force or restrict someone is a synonym of compel.

clue.text: Economise during tour of duty

explanation.surface: Cutting back while serving overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To stint is to be sparing; a stint is also a spell of assigned work.

clue.text: Determined to put the money up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for money is read from bottom to top

parts.note: notes are banknotes, money

explanation.surface: Resolved to stake the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bent on doing something means being determined to do it.

clue.text: Inspected first sardine from a tin

indicators.note: the first letter of the word sardine is taken

parts.note: food from a tin is canned

explanation.surface: Checked the first fish out of a can.
explanation.definitionFit: To look over closely is a synonym of examine or inspect.

clue.text: Hostile to old chaplain in turkey

parts.note: anti means opposed or hostile to
Ch is an abbreviation for chaplain

explanation.surface: An elderly padre has an aversion to the Christmas bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The lower-case 'turkey' disguises the country; the definition 'in turkey' means a place in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient city, now Antakya, located in southern Turkey.

clue.text: Stop providing for many counties in distress

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a lot

indicators.note: letters in distress are knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Aid to many counties in hardship is to cease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' signals an anagram of COUNTIES IN, giving ISCONTINUE after D.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop supplying a product is a synonym of ceasing to provide it.
